key_insight: Halcyon shows that strong text-to-image generation does not require a language-pretrained model. Trained from scratch, Halcyon-0.52B outperforms LlamaGen-XL/8 while using 18.2× less pretraining compute.
problem_solved: Modern text-to-image systems rely on internet-scale language pretraining. This paper tests whether that costly prerequisite is necessary for strong image generation.
method: Introduce Halcyon, a family of early-fusion multimodal autoregressive models.
Pretrain entirely from scratch on GPIC, a dataset of 100 million image-text pairs.
Compare generation quality and pretraining compute: Halcyon-0.52B achieves 48.0 gFD versus LlamaGen-XL/8's 63.3, where lower is better.
impact: The results point to a more compute-efficient route to text-to-image modeling without a separately language-pretrained backbone. Practitioners may be able to simplify training pipelines while maintaining strong generation quality.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: 100M image-text pairs → from-scratch Halcyon training → generated images.
Architecture sketch showing text and image information fused early in an autoregressive model.
Bar chart comparing gFD: Halcyon-0.52B at 48.0 versus LlamaGen-XL/8 at 63.3, labeled 'lower is better.'
Compute-efficiency callout: '18.2× less pretraining compute' alongside 'No language pretraining.'
paper_title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
paper_authors: Keshigeyan Chandrasegaran, Yue Zhao, Armin W. Thomas, Ehsan Adeli, Jiajun Wu
